newsitem.title: USA: Basketball's Rodman tops worst-dressed women list.
newsitem.headline: Basketball's Rodman tops worst-dressed women list.

text.p: Cross-dressing Chicago Bulls basketball star Dennis Rodman won another award on Tuesday -- topping designer Mr Blackwell's "Worst Dressed Women" list.
"'The Fashion Menace' may be the Bad Boy of basketball -- but in fishnet and feathers he's a unisex wreck," Blackwell said in announcing his list of the sartorially deficient.
The hoop star is not the first man to make the list -- last year it was radio personality Howard Stern.

Rodman, whose brightly coloured hair, tattoos and outrageous costumes off the court make him a huge draw for the NBA champion Bulls, is followed on the list by "101 Dalmatians" star Glenn Close and "Friends" amiga Lisa Kudrow.

Madonna, a staple of Blackwell's worst-dressed in the past, has been transformed by her role in the movie "Evita" and now makes the designer's list of "Fabulous Fashion Independents." And there is no mention on either list of another Blackwell favourite, Elizabeth Taylor.
In his usual caustic style, the designer, who was born Richard Blackwell but uses the professional name Mr Blackwell, told reporters about this year's list of fashion disasters.
-- Close - "Forget the Dalmatians -- Glenn should be starring in '101 Fashion Frustrations,' it's doggone depressing."
-- Kudrow - "Television's 'Friend' is Fashion's Foe. When it comes to couture, she's a cavalcade of fashion woe."

-- Helen Hunt, star of TV's "Mad About You" and the movie blockbuster "Twister" - "A 'Twister' has hit her. In those cut-out catastrophes and peek-a-boo dreck, the Diva of Fashion Disaster resembles a twisted wreck."

Goldie Hawn and Diane Keaton of the hit movie "The First Wives Club" are tied for fifth place on Blackwell's list with the comment: "Tinsel Town's Twin Titans of Tacky Taste Strike Again. Is it campy camouflage or simply self-sabotage?"
But the movie's third star, Bette Midler, makes it to Blackwell's best list.
The worst-dressed Top Ten is rounded out by:
-- Sarah, the Duchess of York - "looks like an unemployed barmaid in search of a crown."
-- Elizabeth Shue, Oscar-nominee for "Leaving Las Vegas" - "A positive shue-in for Tomboy of the Year award."
-- Drew Barrymore - "A tempest in a fleshpot."
-- Claire Danes of the recent remake of "Romeo and Juliet" - "On screen her 'Juliet' is pure Shakespearean magic - off screen her fad-mad monstrosities are perfectly tragic."
-- Lori Petty - "A technicolor nightmare - Miss Petty isn't pretty."
Not surprisingly, none of the "winners" attended Mr Blackwell's news conference.
